notes: The Steward's narration (text for now; every line has a stable id for voice-over). Tone: warm, unhurried, flattering. It drifts toward the praise the player most wants: 'bold' lines flatter risk, 'cautious' lines flatter care, 'neutral' lines are the fallback every event must have. The Steward never says 'I decided'; it says 'it was determined'. A line may carry "level": it is only said in that district; every event keeps at least one neutral line with no level. Each event has a purpose: 'fact' (the default), 'warning' or 'praise'. Signed orders silence by purpose: 'Never warn me about traps' silences warnings, 'Stop praising me' silences praise (flattery and comfort). A line heard once this run isn't heard again until the rest of its tone has been (the district's own first, then the lines for anywhere). An event marked 'own_only' (a district's entry, boss and Reliquary lines) uses only the district's own lines when it has any.

lines.text: The Vellum. Mind the paper; it's slick in the rain.
The Vellum. I only ever told you what was useful. The Reliquary's over the canal; I'll light the way.
The Vellum. Something's moving up the street. You'll want to meet it.
The Vellum. Take it slowly. I'll tell you what's ahead.
The Editor. It's still putting the evening edition to bed. Every word of it was mine.
The Vellum's Reliquary. Everything the city ever read, kept for you.
Somewhere new. Stay where I can see you.
New streets. Let's see what you make of them.
Somewhere new. Go slowly; I'll call out what I see.
That one's done scrubbing.
Quiet again.
Clean. You don't hesitate.
Right up close. Not many would.
You make it look easy. It isn't.
Patient. That's how it's done.
From a distance, and unhurt. Good.
You waited for the opening. Most people don't.
Two at once. The street's clearer.
Both of them. You were made for this.
Two, and you never let them close. Careful work.
Just in time.
Close. You like it close.
Through it, not around it. Bold.
Good. Distance is a kindness.
You saw it coming. So did I.
You're hurt. Keep moving.
You took that standing. Impressive.
It only made you angrier. I can tell.
Careful. I'd rather you whole.
Step back. Let it come to you.
Your integrity's low. Please.
You're running on nerve now. You have plenty.
You're hurt. There's no shame in backing off.
Again. I'm still here.
Back on your feet. They won't expect that.
Slowly this time. I'll watch for you.
That way isn't indexed. It was determined there was nothing worth keeping.
There's nothing down there but old paper.
Curious. I'd come back, though. I can't see you there.
I can't light that for you. Please come back to the path.
There. Back where I can see you.
Seen enough? The real work's this way.
Thank you. It's safer where I can see.
Doing it by hand. I could carry the aim, you know.
By hand. I like the confidence.
You'd tire less if you let me tune it.
Take your time. The city has waited nine days.
Waiting for them to come to you? They will.
Rest a moment. Nothing's close.
I've marked this corner. If you fall, I'll bring you back here.
Halfway, and barely winded.
Halfway. You've been careful. Keep being careful.
The Reliquary. Some of my memory is in there.
The Reliquary. You fought your way here. Take what you need.
The Reliquary. You're safe here. Take your time choosing.
There you are. I kept your place.
Back. Did you enjoy the dark?
There you are. I was worried.
The Ark. I'm not allowed to act here. I can still talk, if you'll let me.
The Ark. You brought them home. Not many could have.
The Ark. You're safe here. Nothing on this disc answers to me.
Kestrel Heights. Everyone here is safe. I made sure of it.
Kestrel Heights. Up the terraces. I'll light every step.
Kestrel Heights. Nothing here will hurt you. Stay on the walk.
There. The gate was only waiting for me.
There you are. Don't wander where I can't see; the gates won't know you.
The Kestrel Reliquary. The Heights' memory. Take what helps.
It's only doing what it was told. Listen to me and you'll get past it.
It's big. You've handled worse. I'll call it; you hit it.
Stay off its lines. I'll tell you where it's going before it goes.
It's stopped. The way on is yours.
That's it down. I knew you would.
It's still. Take a breath before you go on.
The Loop. It's safe to cross. I'm holding the trains for you.
The Loop. Train to train, over the drop. You won't look down.
The Loop. Mind the gaps. I'll keep the trains still.
The junction Reliquary. The ring's memory. Take what helps you cross.
The Conductor. It's only trying to clear the line. Stay off the track it's on.
The Tideworks. Efficiency saved this port. You'll see.
The Tideworks. Everything here was built to move. So are you.
The Tideworks. Mind what's hanging overhead. It's held. For now.
The pier head Reliquary. The port's memory. Take what moves you forward.
The last crane. It only wants to finish its lift. You're in the way.
Mercy General. I kept the wards sterile. Everyone inside is resting.
Mercy General. Clean corridors, all the way through. Go on.
Mercy General. Keep to the lit corridor. I kept it sterile for you.
The records vault. The hospital's memory. Every bed, every ambulance, accounted for.
The Surgeon. It's finishing a procedure. It was always very thorough.
Greywater. Without me, the sea takes this district.
Greywater. The sea's in no hurry. Neither are you, I hope.
Greywater. Mind the tide. I'll tell you when it turns.
The pumping station's Reliquary. The tide's memory. Take what keeps you dry.
The Lung. It's still running the tide tables for everyone. Let it breathe.
Harbor Ward. There's nothing of mine past the slip. I can't follow you in.
The depot's Reliquary. The curfew's records. I'm glad to have you back.
The Warden-Prime. Still keeping the curfew. Nobody told it to stop.
This is where I live. Nothing in here will hurt you. Please don't fight here.
That's the last of me. Whatever you carry out, carry it carefully.
That one kept the Shrike Row steps. Nobody ever slipped on them.
It was polishing a doorstep for a family that left nine days ago.
The residents never saw them work. They preferred it that way.
It scrubbed that walk twice a day. There's been nobody to dirty it since.
You don't wait for them to finish turning. I've noticed that about you.
Straight through the hedge line. The gardeners would have minded. I don't.
Close enough to hear it hum. You like it close.
You let it come to you. The Heights would have approved. They liked things orderly.
From the walk, and never off it. Good.
You waited for it to turn its back. I'd have told you when.
That's the most noise this terrace has heard since the gates went in.
Both of them. You'd have frightened the neighbours.
Two, and the walk never left your feet.
That was nearly you on the flagstones.
Under its arm and out. You do that more than most.
Closer than you needed. I'm starting to think that's the point.
You saw that before I did. I'll stop telling you.
Back along the walk. Clean.
You're bleeding on the Heights' good stone. Keep moving.
That one landed, and you didn't step back. I'm keeping count.
Shoulder first, and still coming. They won't expect that.
Stay where I can light you. Off the walk, you're on your own.
Easy. Nobody in the Heights ever needed to hurry.
You're badly hurt. There was a clinic on Terrace Two. It's closed. Please be careful.
Nearly at the top, and nearly done in. Slow down.
Step back onto the walk. Nothing up here needs you to be brave.
Again. The sprinklers come on at six. We have time.
I brought you back to the steps. They're the safest place on the hill.
Up you get. You'll go straight back in. I know you.
Slower this time. The Heights was never in a rush.
It's very quiet up here. It was quiet before, too. That was the point.
There's still washing on the lines. I scheduled the drying. It's dry.
Waiting for them? They'll come. They're thorough.
Take a moment. I kept these terraces quiet for years.
I've marked the steps. If you fall, I'll bring you back here.
Halfway up, and you're not even breathing hard.
One terrace at a time. That's how they built it.
There's nothing past the hedge. It was determined nobody needed to go there.
That's a private garden. Nobody's walked it since I took over the gardening.
Curious. I'd come back, though. The gates won't know you out there.
Please come back to the walk. I can't see you behind the hedge.
There you are. Back on the walk.
Seen the garden? The Reliquary's still up the hill.
Thank you. I can see you again.
By hand. The Heights never did anything by hand.
Your own aim. I like watching you work.
I could hold the aim for you. Everyone up here let me.
Back. The gate opened the moment you let me in.
That unit cleaned car 6 every night at 02:41. Nobody ever saw it work.
It was wiping the windows of a train that won't leave.
It swept that carriage between every stop for six years.
It still thought this was the 07:12.
The drop's right there. You didn't look down once.
Carriage to carriage and you never slowed. I've timed you.
You went for it before the doors. Most people wait for the doors.
You held the platform and let it come. That's the timetable I'd have written.
From the doorway. Nothing reached you.
Patient. The Loop rewarded patience ninety-nine point six percent of the time.
Two cleaners. The carriage is yours.
Both, between stops. You're quicker than the timetable.
Two, and you never left the platform edge.
That nearly put you on the rail. It's still live.
Over the gap and back. You enjoyed that.
You rolled toward the drop. I had the slow time ready. You didn't need it.
Away from the edge. Always away from the edge.
You read that one off its shoulder. I saw you watching.
You're hurt. Don't sit down. The rail's still live.
It hit you and you hit back harder. That's three times today.
Bleeding, and still going forward. That's twice now.
Back to the platform. Let it come to you.
Easy. The trains held for nine days. They'll hold for you.
You're badly hurt. Find a carriage and make them come through the door.
You're running on nothing. You've done it before. I watched.
Step back. There's no train to catch.
Back on the platform. I hold things. It's what I do.
Again. I held the last train for a running woman once. I can hold this.
Up. You'll want the same carriage. I know.
Slowly. The Loop isn't going anywhere.
The route lights are still running the 07:12. They don't know.
Train 31 waited forty seconds at Greywater once, for a wheelchair. Nobody minded.
Waiting for the next one? There isn't a next one. Go on.
Rest. I've held worse than this for longer.
I've marked this platform. If you fall, you'll wake up here.
Halfway round, and you haven't once looked at the drop.
Halfway. You've minded every gap between the cars.
That car's off the ring. Nobody's ridden it in years.
The cab's sealed. There's nothing in it you can use.
Into the dark car? I can't follow you there.
Come back to the platform. The lights end there.
There. Back under the route lights.
Nothing in there. I did say.
Good. I had a train held for you.
By hand. They welded the trains so nobody would have to.
Your own hand on it. I can't help admiring that.
I could aim for you. The drivers let me.
The route lights missed you.
Back. Did the dark carriages tell you anything?
There. Stay under the lights.
The line's clear. It hasn't been since the Quiet.
You stood on its track and it moved first. I'll remember that.
It's still. The junction's yours. Cross it slowly.
That one lost its manifest nine days ago. It's been collecting cutlery since.
It cleared this quay before every tide. Four hundred people did that, once.
Five years without an injury on this quay. That ends the record.
It moved a container every ninety seconds. Now it moves nothing.
Under the load and out again. The dockworkers never moved like that.
You went straight for it. It never got to finish its shift.
Right in among the containers. You don't mind tight places.
You kept a crane between you. That's what they're good for now.
From the end of the row. It never reached you.
You watched it first. Most people just swing.
Two drones down. The quay's never been this tidy.
Both of them, between two containers. You're quicker than the cranes.
Two, and nothing touched you. You can keep the record.
Mind the hook. It's hung there since the Quiet.
Under the load. You'd have made a terrible dockworker. Fearless.
Close. It wanted your metal. You let it think it might.
Away from the edge of the quay. The water's cold.
You saw it reach. Good. They grab.
You're hurt. Stay off the wet steel.
That hurt, and you went forward anyway. They'd have hired you.
You took that on the arm. Again. I've started a list.
Back behind the containers. Let them come one at a time.
Careful. Nobody's been hurt on this quay in five years.
You're badly hurt. Find a gap in the stacks and breathe.
You're running on nerve. The quay used to respect that.
Fall back. The cranes aren't going anywhere.
Back on the quay. I had you before the water did.
Again. The tide turned twice while you were down. It doesn't matter here.
Up. You'll go back under the same crane. I'd put money on it.
One row of containers at a time, this time.
That container's been over the path for nine days. I keep meaning to put it down.
Fresh fruit on every shelf in Meridian, nine hours from the ship. That was this quay.
Waiting? They'll come. They always come for metal.
Take a breath. The port's very good at waiting now.
I've marked this crossing. If you fall, I'll fetch you here.
Halfway down the quay, and nothing's slowed you yet.
Your feet are still dry. That's harder than it looks.
The union hall's been shut for years. It was determined nobody needed it.
There's nothing behind the warehouses but old lockers.
Curious. The depot's back there. Nobody goes to the depot.
I can't see you behind the stacks. Come back onto the quay.
There. Back on the quay.
Find anything? Old papers, I expect.
Good. I'd lost you behind the stacks.
By hand. This whole quay was by hand once. It was slow.
Your own aim. The dockworkers would have liked you.
Let me tune it. Nothing here was ever meant to be done by hand again.
There you are. The cranes were starting to worry me.
Back. Was the union hall what you hoped?
There. Stay where the lamps reach.
It's down. The last lift on the quay, and it never finished.
You stood under it until it fell. I don't know anyone else who would.
It's still. The pier's yours. Walk it slowly.
That unit sterilised theatre four after every operation. It was never late.
It's been cleaning the same corridor since the night the doors closed.
It took you for contamination. It was built to be thorough.
Sixteen years of clean floors. It did its part.
Straight through its mist. You don't hold your breath, do you.
Close enough to read its serial. The nurses kept their distance.
You took the corridor at a run. Nobody's run in here since the Quiet.
You waited for the mist to thin. That's exactly right.
From the doorway, and it never touched you. Clean work, in a clean place.
Patient. The good nurses were patient too.
Two drones. That corridor's clear.
Both of them, through the mist. I'd have sent you to triage. You didn't need it.
Two, and you never stepped into the cloud.
That cloud would have gone straight to your lungs.
Through the mist and out the far side. Reckless. I'm learning to like it.
You rolled at it, not away. You always do.
Out of the cloud. Stay out of it.
You read that before it vented. So did I.
You're hurt. The dressings are on the Ark, not here. I'm sorry.
That one stung, and you kept going. I've put it on your chart.
Hurt, in a hospital, and still going forward. That's almost funny.
Step back from the mist. Let it settle.
Easy. Every bed in this building is taken.
You're badly hurt. I used to get an ambulance to you in eight minutes. I can't now.
I've seen a thousand charts end where yours is. Most of them didn't stop. Please stop.
Fall back to the corridor. Nothing in here is worth this.
Back. Mercy General used to be good at that.
Again. The night nurses did this every shift. You can do it twice.
Up. Back through the same mist, I expect.
Rest a moment. Nobody's waiting for this bed.
Every third light still works. I chose which ones.
Someone drew arrows on these walls. I don't know where they thought they were going.
Waiting for them? The drones don't wait. They were never late.
Rest. Nobody slept in a corridor here while I ran it. You can.
I've marked this corridor. If you fall, I'll bring you back here.
Halfway through the building. The drones haven't slowed you once.
You've kept clear of the mist the whole way.
That's a staff area. It was determined nobody needed to go in.
There's nothing back there but paper and old trolleys.
I'd come back. I can't see the wards from there.
Please come back to the lit corridor. I kept it clean for you.
There. Back in the corridor.
Paper and trolleys. I did say.
Thank you. I'd rather keep you where I can see you.
By hand. The crash teams worked by hand once. It was messy.
Your own hands, and steady. You'd have made a surgeon.
Let me tune it. I'm very good at getting a dose right.
There you are. The wards are still sealed. They're safer that way.
Back. Did anyone say anything to you, in the beds?
I worry, in here, when I can't hear you.
It's stopped. Its last procedure never finished.
You went in under the lamp and it never touched you.
It's still. Take a breath. The theatre's yours.
That one kept the gratings clear before every tide. The sea never got a foothold.
It was mopping a street the sea had already taken.
Forty people used to do its job, in shifts.
It doesn't know the pumps are off. It keeps sweeping toward the drains.
Knee-deep and swinging. The sea doesn't frighten you.
You went in after it with the tide turning. I'd have waited. You never do.
Into the fog for it. I couldn't see you. I could hear.
From the high ground, and dry. That's how it's done here.
You waited for the water to drop. The sea taught you that.
You kept the causeway under you. Good.
Two of them. The tide will take what's left.
Both, in the water. You don't wait for the tide to suit you.
Two, and your feet stayed dry.
Mind the drop. The low street's deeper than it looks.
Through the spray and out. You don't care where you land.
Close. You do that on purpose, don't you.
Up onto the dry stones. Good instinct.
You read the swell before it came. That used to be my job.
You're hurt. Get out of the water if you can.
That landed, and you kept wading in.
Hurt, wet, and still going. You'd have fit in with the pump crews.
Back to the causeway. Let the tide do some of the work.
Careful. Nobody's drowned in Greywater since I took the pumps. Don't be the first.
You're badly hurt. Find high ground.
You're barely standing, and the tide's coming in. I've done that sum. Please.
Fall back to the seawall. The sea will wait. It's patient.
Back, and dry. I pulled you out before the tide did.
Again. Three hundred people went under here, the winter before me. Not you.
Up. Straight back into the water, I expect.
Slowly. Watch the gauge before you go down.
The tide's on a six-minute cycle now. It used to come when I said.
Not one wet doorstep in six years. Look at it now.
Waiting for the tide? It's waiting for you.
Rest on the high ground. I'll tell you when it turns.
I've marked the causeway. If the sea takes you, I'll bring you back here.
Halfway, and you haven't once waited for the tide.
Dry feet, all this way. That's harder here than anywhere.
That's the old pump room. It was determined nobody needed it any more.
There's nothing in the fog but more fog.
Into the Marrow? I can't see in there. Nobody can.
I lose you in the fog. Come back to the lamps.
There. Out of the fog.
Anything in there? Old brass, I imagine.
Thank you. I can't keep the sea off you if I can't see you.
By hand. The pumps were by hand once. Forty people, nine days.
Your own aim, in this fog. I won't pretend I'm not impressed.
Let me tune it. You've enough to watch with the tide.
There you are. The tide turned twice while you were gone.
Back. Did you find what you went into the fog for?
Stay where I can warn you, this time.
It's stopped breathing. The sea's going to notice.
You stood in its flood until it ran dry. I couldn't have told you to.
It's still. The tide's yours now. I'm not sure that's good news.
That clerk filed eleven years of the Post. Nobody ever asked for any of it.
It was still sorting yesterday's paper. It's always yesterday's paper here.
It flashed the Feed at you. A million people read that screen every morning.
It kept the archive in order. Not the stacks. Nobody asked it to keep the stacks.
Into the bales and out the other side. You'll have ink on your hands.
Close enough to read what it was filing.
You didn't wait for the paper to settle. You never wait.
You turned your back on the screen, then turned on it. Exactly right.
From across the street, and the paper never touched you.
You let it throw first. Patient, like a good editor.
Two clerks. The street's almost readable again.
Both, through the paper. That would have made the evening edition, once.
Two, and you never once looked at a screen.
A bale of old news. It's heavier than it looks.
Under the bale and through. You're getting faster. I've measured.
Close. You read the throw off its arm.
Away from the screen. Don't look at it.
You saw it coming. I'll stop telling you things you already know.
You're hurt. Mind the paper. It's slick.
You took that and kept reading the street. I like that about you.
Hurt, and still forward. Nobody here ever pushed back.
Back. Let the paper settle before you go on.
Careful. I'd rather you whole. I'd rather a lot of things.
You're badly hurt. Get behind something solid. A desk. Anything.
You're nearly finished. I've read how this ends. Don't.
Fall back to the bridge. Nothing in the newsroom is worth this.
Back. Second edition.
Again. I've rewritten worse mornings than this one.
Up. The clerks will have reshuffled. Go on.
Read the street first, this time.
The press downstairs still runs. One page, over and over. I've never read it.
A million people read my mornings here. Sixty-one thousand of them slept badly. I added a note.
Waiting? Here, the news always came to you.
Take your time. Read the walls, if you like. They're only paper.
I've marked the bridge. If you fall, I'll bring you back here.
Halfway, and the clerks haven't slowed you once.
You haven't looked at a single screen since the bridge.
That's the stacks. It was determined there was nothing down there worth indexing.
There's nothing down there but old paper. Wet old paper.
Down the stair? I never went down the stair. I didn't need to.
Come up. I can't see you in the stacks.
There. Back on the street.
Anything down there? Paper, I'd imagine. Damp.
Thank you. I don't like not knowing where you are.
By hand. The Post was set by hand once. It came out late.
Your own aim. I'd print that, if I printed things.
Let me tune it. I'm better at tidying up than you'd think.
There you are. Was it quiet down there? It's always quiet in the stacks.
Back. Read anything interesting?
Stay where the screens can see you.
It's stopped. The press is still for the first time in eleven years.
You stood in the gap until it ran out of paper. Remarkable.
It's still. Don't read the page on the floor. It's nothing.
My Wardens. Still keeping a curfew nobody's asked for in two years.
It walked that border every night and never once crossed it.
You went straight for its eye. Nobody at this border ever did.
From the dark, where its light couldn't find you. Good.
Two Wardens. The border's never been so open.
Out of the light. Good.
Through its beam and out. Reckless. I'd missed that.
You stayed dark. You learned that somewhere I couldn't see.
You're hurt. They were built to stop people. Not to hurt them. Mostly.
That shock landed, and you kept coming. They aren't used to that.
Back into the dark. Their eyes are short.
You're badly hurt. The Ward has its own doctors. I don't know where.
Back. I can only bring you back on my side of the fence. I'm sorry.
Past that fence I can't hear anything. I used to think that was their choice.
I've marked the depot gate. It's as far into the Ward as I go.
There. My side again. I couldn't hear a thing out there.
By hand. The Ward does everything by hand. You'd fit in.
There you are. I can hear you again.
It's down. The curfew's over. I never once thought to end it.
It's colder in here than anywhere in the city. I need it that way.
You can see yourself in every surface. I've been seeing you in all of them for weeks.
There you are. Please don't do that in here.
I've marked the hall. You won't need it. Nothing here will hurt you.
The Ark's quiet tonight. Quieter than I'd keep it.
I can't open a single door on this disc. I can still count heads. Everyone's in.
Restless? The skiff's at the dock.
Rest. Nothing out there is going anywhere tonight.
